class.name: UZUJuice
class.brief_description: Game feel effects (hitstop, slow motion, and more) behind single static calls.
class.description: [UZUJuice] is U.ZU Engine's game-feel toolkit: the small effects that make actions feel good, callable in one line from anywhere. A runtime node is created in the scene tree on first use and drives the effects by wall-clock deadlines, so durations are real seconds regardless of the time scale the effects themselves set. This class currently provides the time effects: [method hitstop] and [method slowmo]. While an effect is active, UZUJuice owns [member Engine.time_scale]; when the last effect ends, the scale that was in place before the first effect started is restored. A running hitstop wins over a running slow motion. [codeblock] # A heavy hit: freeze for a blink, with the matching sound (UZUSfx). UZUJuice.hitstop(0.06) UZUSfx.play(self, UZUSfx.generate_preset("hit")) # A near miss: a moment of slow motion. UZUJuice.slowmo(0.25, 0.4) [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] This class is specific to U.ZU Engine (UZUJuice, BACKLOG Phase 11).

method.name: applied_time_scale
method.description: The time scale UZUJuice is applying right now: the hitstop scale while a hitstop runs, else the slow-motion scale while one runs, else the scale that was in place before the effects started (1.0 when nothing ever ran).

method.name: cancel_time_effects
method.description: Ends all running time effects immediately and restores the time scale from before they started.

method.name: hitstop
method.description: Freezes the game's time for [param duration] real seconds, running it at [param scale] meanwhile (0.0 is a full stop; a small value like 0.05 keeps a hint of motion). The classic pause that sells a hit landing. If a slow motion is running, the hitstop takes over and the slow motion resumes afterwards if its duration has not elapsed.

method.name: is_time_effect_active
method.description: True while a hitstop or slow motion is still running.

method.name: slowmo
method.description: Runs the game's time at [param scale] (for example 0.25) for [param duration] real seconds, then restores the previous scale.

method.name: clear_shake
method.description: Stops the screen shake immediately and restores the camera's own offset exactly.

method.name: get_trauma
method.description: The current shake trauma (0..1). The applied offset scales with trauma squared, so a trauma of 0.5 shakes a quarter as much as 1.0.

method.name: shake
method.description: Adds [param amount] of screen-shake trauma (clamped to 1.0 in total): about 0.3 for a normal hit, 0.7 for a big explosion. Trauma decays at 1.6 per second on its own. The shake is applied to the current camera (Camera3D h/v offset or Camera2D offset), preserving and later restoring the camera's own offset.

method.name: flash
method.description: Tints [param node] toward [param color] and fades back over [param duration] seconds, restoring the node exactly. Works on [CanvasItem]s and [Sprite3D] (their modulate) and on other [GeometryInstance3D]s (a fading material overlay). Flashing the same node again restarts the flash from the new color, keeping the original base.

method.name: squash
method.description: Squashes [param node] (a [Node2D] or [Node3D]) flat by [param amount] and lets a spring bring it back with a wobble, roughly preserving volume (wider as it gets flatter). The node's own scale is captured and restored exactly when the spring settles.

method.name: burst2d
method.description: Spawns a one-shot burst of [param count] particles at [param global_position] under [param parent], flying outward and falling, in [param color]; the node frees itself when the burst ends. [param power] scales the speed and the lifetime. The particles use a small generated dot texture, so no assets are needed.

method.name: burst3d
method.description: The 3D form of [method burst2d]: billboarded quads in [param color], world-space (they do not follow the parent after spawning).

method.name: get_kick
method.description: The current camera-kick displacement (0 when settled).

method.name: kick
method.description: Punches the current camera's zoom: a Camera3D's field of view dips by up to 8 × [param amount] degrees (a Camera2D's zoom rises by up to 25 × [param amount] percent) and a spring brings it back. The camera's own field of view / zoom is captured and restored exactly.
